chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them all). He said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) saw a man from his Shi'a after a long time, and aging had left its mark on him. He was persevering in his walk. So he said: You have aged, O man. He said: In obedience to you, O Commander of the Faithful. So he said: You are still enduring. He said: Against your enemies, O Commander of the Faithful. So he said: I find remaining strength in you. He said: It is for you, O Commander of the Faithful.

key_terms.بقية: Remaining strength/energy - whatever life force is left
key_terms.طاعتك: Obedience to you - devotion and service to the Imam
key_terms.يتجلد: Persevering/enduring despite difficulty - showing fortitude in old age

ai.seo_question: What is the famous dialogue between Imam Ali and his elderly Shia follower about loyalty?
ai.summary: This beautiful dialogue between Imam Ali (peace be upon him) and an elderly Shi'a follower is narrated through the golden chain (silsilat al-dhahab) of all the Imams from al-Husayn back through al-Rida. After a long absence, Imam Ali encounters an aging follower who struggles to walk but perseveres. In a three-part exchange, each of the Imam's observations about the man's condition is met with a reply of selfless devotion: his age was spent in obedience, his endurance directed against the Imam's enemies, and whatever strength remains is dedicated to the Imam. This hadith exemplifies the Shia ideal of walaya (loyalty) and the total dedication a follower shows to the Imam.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from his father from al-Rayyan b. al-Salt from al-Rida `Ali b. Musa from his father Musa b. Ja`far from his father Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father Muhammad b. `Ali from his father `Ali b. al-Husayn from his father al-Husayn b. `Ali (as). He said:

Amir al-Mu’minin (as) saw a man from his Shi`a after a long time [away from him], and the signs of aging were visible on him. He had a limp in his walk. So, he (as) said: O man! You have aged. He said: In obedience to you, O Amir al-Mu’minin. So, he (as) said: You are limping. He said: Due to your enemies, O Amir al-Mu’minin. So, he (as) said: I see some strength in you. He said: It is for you, O Amir al-Mu’minin.
